blocks.text: Pliny, Hist. Nat. book 10, ch. 42, §. 58, writes that the parrot is called Sittace in India. Reland, in Dissertatt. Miscellann. vol. 1, p. 184, thinks this name was formed from Tedac, and this from חך: "whether," he says, "others made تدك [tdk] from חך by doubling the first letter, or by adding a letter of similar sound, or whether חך arose from Tedac by dropping one of the first two letters because of their similarity of sound." How slippery and uncertain this is, anyone will see for himself. I pass over the dreams of others about this word; whoever wishes to know them may consult Simonis, Lexic., under the word. For my part, I think we should rest content with what Bochart has argued here no less acutely than learnedly.
Pliny, book 11, ch. 38: "Peacocks have crests on the head, made of hairy little tree-like tufts."
